changes.text:
Following up on the work-acceptance record. The draft profile and five CC0 vectors are now at https://github.com/maximusrufus/work-acceptance-record:

- 01 valid, independent, criteria committed first
- 02 criteria committed after the issue time
- 03 self-checked
- 04 a required criterion `not-evaluated`, which gives `incomplete`
- 05 checker key equal to producer key

Each vector carries its inputs and an `expected` object (signature, file and criteria binding, criteria-before-check, independence, recomputed verdict, problem and warning codes). It's JCS plus Ed25519 plus an RFC 3161 imprint.

@Johnny-Kao — this is the exact gap `delegation_chain_ref` (argentum-core) is built for: B shouldn't rely on A's assertion at all. A's request would carry a chain artifact recording root_delegator → ... → A, each hop with its own `delegation_ref` and `scope`. B (or anyone) recomputes and verifies the chain independently — confirms each hop's `delegation_ref`, confirms continuity (each `delegatee` equals the next hop's `delegator`), and checks whether the scope at A's hop actually covers the specific payment being requested, instead of trusting A's say-so.

We implemented the single-payment part of this draft (§6, §7) in presign-guard, a pre-sign check for agent payments:

- POST /v1/check takes an optional mandate next to an EIP-3009 signature and turns a payment outside it red before the agent signs (wrong payer/asset/recipient, over perPayment or cap, expired, bad issuer signature, nonce ≠ binding).
- presign-guard-wallet's mandatePayer() makes x402 payments with the §7 binding as the EIP-3009 nonce.
- JCS bytes, digest, signature and the EIP-3009/Permit2 binding values match authority-vectors.json byte for byte.

Not covered: cumulative spend
